title: Sponsor Job Titles — Create / Edit
overviewHtml: How many employees a sponsor may have under one government job title, split between citizens and non-citizens. The two percentages must add up to 100. Allowed places are worked out on save: citizens get the number of positions times their percentage rounded down, non-citizens rounded up. An employee sponsor record can only be added for a job title the sponsor has a row for. Remaining places are shown on the Sponsor Job Title Quota Report; nothing stops the quota being exceeded.

fields.label: GovtJobTitle
fields.rules: Required. Chosen from Govt Job Title master data.
fields.html:
What it is. The government job title.

Example. Accountant

fields.label: StartDate
fields.html: What it is. The first day this record applies.

fields.label: EndDate
fields.rules: Required. Date value. Cannot be before the start date.
fields.html: What it is. The last day this record applies.

fields.label: NoofPosition
fields.html:
What it is. The total number of positions allowed.

Example. 20

fields.label: CitizenPercent
fields.html:
What it is. The share of positions for citizens.

Example. 30

fields.label: CitizenQuotaUsed
fields.html:
What it is. How many places are taken by citizens.

Why it matters. Goes up by one when an employee sponsor record is added for an employee whose nationality group is Citizen, and down by one when one is deleted. Changing a record does not recount it.

fields.label: NonCitizenPercent
fields.html:
What it is. The share of positions for non-citizens.

Example. 70

fields.label: NonCitizenQuotaUsed
fields.html:
What it is. How many places are taken by non-citizens.

Why it matters. Goes up and down the same way, for employees in any other nationality group.
